title: 2025 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: The polynomial \((z + i)(z + 2i)(z + 3i) + 10\) has three roots in the complex plane, where \(i = \sqrt{-1}.\) What is the area of the triangle formed by these roots?

solutions.text:
The sum of the roots is \(-6i,\) so the centroid is \(-2i.\) Substituting \(z = u - 2i,\) \[ \begin{gathered} (u - i)(u)(u + i) + 10 \\ = u(u^2 + 1) + 10 \\ = u^3 + u + 10. \end{gathered} \]

Since \(u = -2\) is a root, \(u^3 + u + 10\) \(= (u + 2)(u^2 - 2u + 5),\) giving roots \(u = -2\) and \(u = 1 \pm 2i.\)

These are the points \((-2, 0),\) \((1, 2),\) \((1, -2).\) The base between \((1, 2)\) and \((1, -2)\) has length \(4,\) at horizontal distance \(3\) from \((-2, 0),\) so the area is \(\dfrac{1}{2}(4)(3) = 6.\) Translation does not change the area.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Shift by the centroid: let \(z = u - 2i\) to center the roots at the origin
